title: PowerPoint on Mac: reference webpages when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: the briefing overstates what is known about controlling and auditing this PowerPoint feature, and omits important exceptions to the general web-search rules. The roadmap details and general control references are accurate, but several statements that Microsoft has not described the behaviour are contradicted by the cited release notes.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The Mac release note says Copilot gathers relevant information from the web and uses referenced sources during presentation creation.
claims.quote: This update enables Copilot to gather relevant information from the web and use referenced sources while respecting web content security and privacy standards.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The release note says this respects web content security and privacy standards.
claims.quote: while respecting web content security and privacy standards.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: No standalone Microsoft Learn page for this specific Mac webpage-reference feature was found.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode reference webpages Mac default license pricing admin policy web search; Copilot PowerPoint reference online sources presentation web search queries policy. Opened release-notes and Copilot requirements; results document the release or separate Copilot-app agents.

claims.claim: The roadmap description and this release note do not say whether users paste webpage addresses.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint reference webpages license pricing default setting; Copilot PowerPoint reference online sources presentation web search queries policy. Read roadmap 555893 and its release-notes entry: neither describes pasting addresses.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor the release note says users can ask Copilot to find sources.
claims.quote: You can now ask Copilot in PowerPoint to reference relevant online sources while creating a presentation. ... Ask Copilot to create a presentation on a topic that would benefit from current web information. ... Review the generated slides and source references.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence about asking Copilot to find sources with: 'The release note tells users to ask Copilot to create a presentation on a topic that benefits from current web information and review the generated slides and source references.' Narrow the corresponding open question to user-supplied addresses and whether references are embedded in the generated deck.

claims.claim: The release-note entry for this roadmap item does not use the words Agent Mode.
claims.quote: Searched: 555893 in the fetched Microsoft 365 Copilot release-notes page; read the complete matching Mac entry. It names Copilot in PowerPoint and source referencing, not Agent Mode.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Copilot web search generates a search query from prompt terms and sends it to Bing.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: The risk section states without qualification that web search sends a generated query, not the full prompt.
claims.quote: The following information isn't included in the generated search query sent to the Bing search service: ... The user's entire prompt, unless the prompt is very short (for example, "local weather")
claims.fix: In the first Data exposure bullet, replace 'a generated query, not the full prompt' with 'a generated query, which can contain the entire prompt when the prompt is very short'. Keep the existing exception in Why it matters.

claims.claim: Generated web-search queries exclude entire Microsoft 365 files.
claims.quote: The following information isn't included ... Entire Microsoft 365 files (for example, emails or documents) or files uploaded into Copilot

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A query can be informed by data in a document when a user prompts Copilot inside a Microsoft 365 app.
claims.quote: it may also be informed by data within a Microsoft 365 document ... When a user enters a prompt into Copilot inside a Microsoft 365 application (for example, writing a prompt into Copilot in Microsoft Word while a relevant document is open).

claims.claim: Copilot sends the user's client IP address with a Bing web-search request.
claims.quote: When Copilot sends a web search request to the Bing search service, it also sends the user's client IP address

claims.claim: Bing operates separately from Microsoft 365 with different data-handling terms.
claims.quote: The Bing search service operates separately from Microsoft 365 and has different data-handling practices.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Microsoft Data Protection Addendum does not apply to generated web-search queries.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum (DPA) doesn't apply to the use of generated web search queries in Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Chat, or the Bing search service.

claims.claim: HIPAA compliance does not apply to generated search queries.
claims.quote: Also, HIPAA compliance and the EU Data Boundary don't apply to generated search queries.

claims.claim: The EU Data Boundary does not apply to generated search queries.
claims.quote: Also, HIPAA compliance and the EU Data Boundary don't apply to generated search queries.

claims.claim: No source says existing behaviour changes.
claims.quote: Previously, users could not directly incorporate live web information as source material within Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.fix: Replace 'Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival for this feature, so no source says existing behaviour changes' with 'Microsoft has not stated the feature-specific default on arrival. The release note does describe a new capability: users previously could not directly incorporate live web information as source material within Copilot in PowerPoint.'

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode reference webpages Mac default license pricing admin policy web search; 555893 default license control PowerPoint. Read roadmap, matching release entry, configure-copilot-admin-center and requirements: no feature-specific automatic-enablement default.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: General Copilot web search is available whenever Allow web search in Copilot is not configured.
claims.quote: web search will be available ... unless the IT admin has set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Disabled.
claims.fix: Replace both unqualified default statements with: 'For the Worldwide cloud in this record, Copilot web search is available when Allow web search in Copilot is not configured, unless Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office is Disabled.' The later discussion of that exception should remain consistent.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is an appropriate role for managing Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center, use an appropriate admin role, such as AI Administrator.

claims.claim: Creating Cloud Policy settings for Microsoft 365 apps requires the Office Apps admin role.
claims.quote: creating Cloud Policy settings for Microsoft 365 apps requires the Office Apps admin role.

claims.claim: General Copilot web-search query logging supports search, audit and eDiscovery.
claims.quote: Web search query logging is available so that admins can perform search, audit, and eDiscovery on the exact web search queries Copilot derived from the user's prompt.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot is a Cloud Policy control for users or user groups across a tenant, covering Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: This policy allows IT admins to either turn on or turn off web search for users or user groups across the tenant they manage ... This policy applies to both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > Data access > Web search for Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat reaches the documented shortcut to the cloud policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, expand Copilot, and then select Settings. ... Configure data access ... Web search for Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat ... Follow the link from Copilot settings to create an Allow web search in Copilot cloud policy

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can set the general web-search control using applyOnce and microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors ... mode ... The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue. ... applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.
claims.fix: Keep the method and path. Add to controls[0].note and its rendered copy: 'The baseline resource microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch sets properties.value (string); "0" enables web search in both experiences, "1" disables it in both, and "2" disables it in Work mode only.' These names and values are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-copilot-resources#allowwebsearch-resource-type.

claims.claim: The Graph Tenant Configuration Management route is preview.
claims.quote: These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: TCM supports these Copilot settings only in tenant-level policies; a group-level policy configuring the same setting makes the resource operation fail.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies ... ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy ... If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: No feature-specific UI or API switch for referencing webpages in PowerPoint Agent Mode on Mac is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode reference webpages admin switch Microsoft Graph Cloud Policy; PowerPoint Agent Mode reference webpages Mac default license pricing admin policy web search. Read Copilot settings, TCM Copilot resources and release entry: no separate webpage-reference switch.

Read roadmap, release entry, copilot-overview and copilot-license-options: no separate price, meter or credit rate for this capability.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics are not stated.
claims.quote: It includes changes that are generally available (Current Channel for Microsoft 365 apps) ... Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.
claims.fix: Replace the rollout-mechanics and release-channel portion with: 'The release-notes page describes generally available changes for Current Channel and gradual deployment to subsets of users before expanding across a tenant; it gives no Mac feature-specific build or rollout window.' Retain only the narrower unresolved feature-specific prerequisites.

claims.claim: The roadmap description and matching release entry describe no actions beyond creating the presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: 555893 in fetched release-notes; read its complete entry and roadmap description. The entry describes gathering web information, creating slides and reviewing source references, not sending or publishing the presentation or other external actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: When general Copilot web search is enabled by an admin, users can still turn it off.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns on web search for Microsoft Copilot users, those users still have the option to turn off web search by using the Web content toggle.

claims.claim: When an admin disables general web search, the Web content toggle is off and dimmed and users cannot enable it.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns off web search, the Web content toggle is turned off and appears dimmed. Users can't turn on the toggle to use web search.

claims.claim: The user web-search toggle is in Microsoft Copilot app > Settings > Personalization > Advanced > Web search.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Copilot app, open Settings, and then select Personalization. ... Expand Advanced, and turn off the Web search toggle.

claims.claim: Disabling optional connected experiences turns off web search when its own policy is unconfigured, but restricts other Microsoft 365 experiences too.
claims.quote: unless the IT admin has set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Disabled. But turning off optional connected experiences restricts Microsoft Copilot Chat, Microsoft Copilot, and multiple experiences across Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Mac PowerPoint users can use the Copilot app toggle to switch off web sourcing for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint web search Copilot policy; PowerPoint Agent Mode reference webpages Mac default license pricing admin policy web search. Read manage-public-web-access, requirements and the release entry: no statement connecting this feature's webpage references to the app toggle.
claims.fix: Replace the toggle advice with: 'Tell Mac PowerPoint users that Copilot-generated decks can contain web-sourced content. Before presenting the Copilot app's Settings > Personalization > Advanced > Web search toggle as a control for this feature, confirm that it governs this webpage-reference flow.'

claims.claim: General web-search query logs can be reviewed to audit groups using this particular PowerPoint feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference online sources presentation web search queries policy; PowerPoint web search Copilot policy. Read manage-public-web-access and release entry: general query audit exists, but this flow's logged events or source-to-query mapping are not identified.
claims.fix: Replace the audit checklist bullet with: 'Confirm whether this PowerPoint webpage-reference flow generates the documented Copilot web-search query logs before relying on Microsoft Purview audit or eDiscovery to review its use.'

claims.claim: This specific feature is a new route for prompt content to leave the Microsoft 365 boundary.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference online sources presentation web search queries policy; PowerPoint web search Copilot policy. Read release entry and manage-public-web-access: external queries are documented for general web search, not the transport used by this new webpage-reference flow.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'If this feature uses Copilot web search, generated search queries can carry information derived from prompts to the Bing search service outside Microsoft 365.'

claims.claim: General web search is off by default for GCC and DoD customers.
claims.quote: For United States government customers using Microsoft 365 (or Office 365) Government Community Cloud (GCC) or DoD offerings: ... Web search is available, but is turned off by default.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist instructs users to set the web-search toggle, but that control has no row in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'they can switch off the Web content toggle in the Microsoft Copilot app'. Table rows: 'Whether Copilot web search is available to users or groups'; 'Switch for referencing webpages in PowerPoint Agent Mode on Mac'.
claims.fix: Remove the instruction to set the user toggle from the rollout checklist, retaining it only as general background or a control whose applicability must first be confirmed. Do not add a controls row.

claims.claim: Whether source references are embedded in the generated deck remains undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference online sources presentation web search queries policy. Read matching release entry: 'Review the generated slides and source references' establishes reviewable references, but not their placement in the generated deck.

claims.claim: The release channel is not stated.
claims.quote: It includes changes that are generally available (Current Channel for Microsoft 365 apps) and specific to each platform.
claims.fix: Replace the release-channel absence with: 'The release-notes page describes generally available changes for Current Channel; it gives no Mac feature-specific build.'
